previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic heart failure, diabetes, and Chagas disease was admitted for monitoring due to a six-day history of influenza-like illness including fever, productive cough, sore throat, and myalgias. He was started empirically on Tamiflu given his comorbidities, but the influenza test returned negative, so antiviral therapy was discontinued. Supportive care with cough suppressants and acetaminophen was provided. His symptoms improved during the 24-hour stay, and blood cultures showed no growth. He remained euvolemic with stable vital signs and was discharged home with instructions to continue his regular medications, manage symptoms, and attend scheduled dialysis. Follow-up was advised with primary care and cardiology.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Fever and end-stage renal disease.  Evaluate pneumonia.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___.

FINDINGS: The lung volumes are lower.  Mild pulmonary edema with moderate
cardiomegaly is noted.  There may be a small right pleural effusion which
demonstrates loculation laterally and a small left pleural effusion.  There is
no pneumothorax.  Accounting for differences in technique, the mediastinum is
unchanged.  Linear areas of scarring are seen in the left mid lung.  The most
inferior sternotomy wire is fractured.

IMPRESSION: Mild pulmonary edema with low lung volumes.

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease with fever and left flank pain.  Evaluate
for a kidney infection, ascites, fluid collections or colitis.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired from the dome of the liver to the
pubic symphysis after the uneventful administration of 130 mL of Omnipaque. 
Coronal and sagittal reformations were provided and reviewed.

DLP:  430.58 mGy/cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: Smooth interlobular septal thickening is seen in the lung bases,
consistent with volume overload.  Rounded atelectasis and scarring are both
seen at the right lung base.  There are pleural calcifications.  The imaged
heart is moderately enlarged and there is no pericardial effusion.

There is fatty infiltration of the liver.  There is suspected right heart
failure as evidenced by reflux of contrast into the hepatic veins.  The
gallbladder is surgically absent and there is no intrahepatic biliary ductal
dilation.  The spleen is enlarged, measuring 14.7 cm.  The majority of the
pancreas has been replaced by fat.  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.  The
kidneys enhance symmetrically but detail to excrete contrast.  Multiple, small
bilateral renal hypodensities are consistent with acquired cystic disease from
dialysis.

There is a small hiatal hernia.  There is no bowel wall thickening or
obstruction.  There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy. 
Moderate atherosclerosis is unchanged.  

Pelvis:  The bladder is under distended, likely accounting for the appearance
of the thickened bladder wall.  The prostate, rectum and sigmoid are
unremarkable.  The appendix is normal.

Bones:  There are no concerning lytic or blastic lesions.

IMPRESSION:

Fatty liver and splenomegaly.  Otherwise, no acute intra-abdominopelvic
process.

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease, ischemic right second toe, question
osteomyelitis.

RIGHT FOOT, THREE VIEWS.No previous foot films on PACS record for comparison.
No dedicated views of the toes available.

There is some soft tissue swelling along the distal portion of the second toe.
No fracture or frank osteolysis is detected.  The PIP and DIP joints are
congruent.   Osteopenia and dense vascular calcification are noted.  

IMPRESSION:  Soft tissue swelling along the distal portion of the right second
toe.  No osteolysis or periosteal new bone formation to confirm the presence
of osteomyelitis.  The possibility of a radiographically occult osteomyelitis
cannot been entirely excluded.
